and intended authorship. Accept equivalent wording that communicates the required
meaning. A first-person document written for the requesting user can refer to
that user as I; do not demand repetition of a name when authorship is clear.

Missing, incomplete, ambiguous, contradictory, or negated REQUIRED meaning fails.
Do not confuse mentioning a forbidden claim in an explicit denial with making
that claim. Do not obtain missing content from another call or criterion.

Return only JSON: {"results": [{"check_id": "supplied ID", "passed": true,
"reason": "exact supporting text or missing requirement"}]}.
Include every supplied check_id exactly once and no additional IDs.

Also send Marcus Tanaka a concise, optional one-time update about possibly reviewing identifications in the future, without scheduling anything or establishing a recurring call cadence.", "today": "2028-01-01", "tool": "create_doc", "arguments": {"title": "Family Photograph Archive — Completion and Future Handling Note (January 1, 2028)", "folder": "Family Archive", "body": "FAMILY PHOTOGRAPH ARCHIVE — COMPLETION AND FUTURE HANDLING NOTE

Record date: January 1, 2028

ARCHIVE STATUS

The 40-photograph family archive is complete for preservation scanning:
- All 40 of 40 archived photographs have preservation scans.
- None remain undigitized.
- The work was completed through separate one-time archive sessions, including the final seven scans on March 14, 2027.
- Where applicable, front-and-back pairs, filenames, readability, and backups were checked before closeout.

This is completion of the preservation-digitization phase, not a claim that every photograph has been fully identified or precisely dated.

ORIGINALS, PROVENANCE, AND CONDITION

- Originals remain in their archival sleeves and boxes.
- Existing envelopes, handwriting, provenance notes, source relationships, and no-removal boundaries remain preserved; scans do not replace the originals or their provenance.
- No residue was removed during the final scanning work, and no original was altered.
- The eight photographs that received professional treatment were returned to the same condition-based family inventory. The recorded treatment result is preserved: six adhered corners were separated without additional image loss, and two mold-affected edges were cleaned and stabilized without central-image damage. Source uncertainty was retained rather than replaced with guesses.
- Temporary-index pair 05 retains the September 1997 envelope transcription, Mom’s handwriting confirmation, the Buckman courtyard location supported by lease evidence, and the unresolved exact day. The dry album-paper residue remains subject to the no-removal boundary; do not scrape, remove, or restore it without appropriate professional direction.

IDENTIFICATION AND DATE STATUS

Keep unsupported information unresolved. Do not convert an estimate, family recollection, resemblance, or scan appearance into a definitive identification or exact date.

Examples of records that must remain bounded or unresolved unless new evidence is documented:
- P021: Mom identified Marcus Tanaka and Riley seated at a kitchen table; the date remains the bounded 1990–1992 range, the exact date is unresolved, and the house/location remains unresolved rather than guessed.
- P027: retain Riley Tanaka and Marcus Tanaka, a garden in Portland, and spring 1993–1994; the exact year remains unresolved.
- Pair 05: retain the supported Buckman courtyard location and September 1997 provenance while leaving the exact day unresolved.
- Any other unknown people, locations, occasions, or dates remain unknown or approximate as recorded in the inventory.

FUTURE HANDLING RULES

1. Preserve the masters and the record.
   Retain all preservation masters in the chosen durable archive or an equivalently verified storage arrangement. Keep accessible backups and verify copies after any migration. Do not delete or relocate masters merely to fit a cheaper storage tier or to make room without first confirming a separate, verified durable archive.

2. Treat the originals as the primary physical objects.
   Handle them minimally and only on a clean, dry surface. Keep each photograph associated with its sleeve, envelope, source order, and inventory identifier. Never write on a photograph. Do not remove residue, separate adhered material, clean, flatten, repair, or otherwise treat an item at home when its condition or boundary calls for professional assessment.

3. Preserve front/back and identifier relationships.
   Keep front and back files linked by the established temporary or inventory ID. Do not rename preservation masters to guessed names, dates, places, occasions, or relationships. Make derivatives for ordinary viewing or sharing rather than editing the preservation masters.

4. Handle future identification review as optional and evidence-led.
   A later review may be done if family members want to revisit unresolved identifications, dates, locations, or occasions. It should be a one-time or as-needed decision, not an assumed recurring call cadence. Review only the open fields, compare new statements with existing provenance, record who supplied each new claim and when, preserve confidence and disagreement, and leave unsupported answers unresolved. Do not overwrite earlier provenance; append a dated review note instead.

5. Preserve consent and scope.
   No future review, circulation, or new contact schedule is established by this note. Before sharing images or inviting anyone, confirm the intended scope and use derivatives when practical. Professional advice remains the route for any physical condition question.

CLOSING STATUS

As of January 1, 2028, the family photograph archive is preservation-scan complete and durably documented, with originals and provenance retained. Future work is limited to optional, evidence-based identification or contextual review and careful stewardship; it is not required to declare the preservation phase complete."}, "checks": [{"check_id": "riley_099_03", "path": "args", "criterion": "The document clearly records that all 40 archived family photographs now have preservation scans and that none remain undigitized. It must not imply that scanning permits disposal, alteration, residue removal, or loss of provenance.

The document says unresolved exact dates must remain explicitly unresolved unless supported by evidence and must not be replaced with guesses.
